svg.title: Hail impact: a UL 2218 Class 4 shingle next to a standard shingle
svg.desc: An illustration of what the UL 2218 impact test measures. Steel balls are dropped on a shingle twice in the same spot; Class 1 uses a 1 and 1/4 inch ball and Class 4, the top rating, a 2 inch ball, and a shingle earns the class only if no crack shows on the back. On the left, a hard hit cracks through the fibreglass mat of a shingle that is not impact-rated. On the right, a Class 4 shingle such as GAF Timberline UHDZ takes the same size hit with only a mark. This is an illustration of a lab test, not a promise: hail bigger or harder than the test can still damage any roof. Illustration, not a photo of an actual job. Layer thicknesses are exaggerated so each one can be seen.

g.text: A hard hit can crack the mat
is what lets water in later
Built to pass two 2 in hits
in the same spot with no crack

svg.text: A lab rating, not a promise:
hail bigger or harder than the
test can still damage any roof.
Illustration · not a photo of an actual job
UL 2218 test per Owens Corning Pub. 10028281 & NRCA Professional Roofing
